correctness.rationale: The Fourier map is a bijection to quadratic q(y)=1-ay+by^2. For all r>0 the unique h and z exist by strict monotonicity. The analytic derivative has precisely two interior roots 1/z,h/z, with the endpoints yielding exact +,-,+ alternating signed extrema. Every non-better competitor differs by y times an affine function whose signs at these three contacts violate affine interpolation unless it vanishes identically. Therefore the unique global optimizer and full claimed bound are proved for all positive orders. Coefficient conversion and fifth-order evaluation are verified by freshly executed CHECK.py; sampled experiments do not bear the universal proof.

value.rationale: At five sites the symmetric normalization leaves two free Fourier coefficients, the first multivariate case beyond solved three-point smoothing. The formula determines an exact globally optimal norm and unique kernel at all finite positive orders, including previously open unrestricted orders k≥4 at this natural radius. The strict negative Fourier lobe proves the difference from Fourier-positive optimizations; the three-contact geometry supplies reusable structure. It is not a generic asymptotic, numerical sample or unmotivated parameter slice. Larger radii remain open.
